tagline: A premium East End water network across Peconic & Gardiners Bays — short island crossings plus a Montauk–Block Island offshore hero leg
summary: Long Island's East End is one of the highest-wealth leisure markets in the US, and its bays are already a working ferry network. North Ferry and South Ferry shuttle continuously across to Shelter Island, Cross Sound Ferry runs vehicles from Orient Point to New London, and the Viking Fleet runs a seasonal Montauk–Block Island express. Suffolk County's March 2026 study is actively scoping a public passenger ferry linking Sag Harbor, Greenport, Orient and Montauk — a greenfield public corridor anchored at Sag Harbor's Long Wharf. Short protected crossings (Sag Harbor ↔ Shelter Island ~3 nm, Sag Harbor ↔ Greenport ~6 nm) are ideal high-frequency foiling shuttles, while Montauk ↔ Block Island (~14 nm) and Sag Harbor ↔ Montauk (~20 nm) are open-water hero legs squarely inside the Pioneer II's 70-nm range — and far faster by water than the gridlocked summer drive out the South Fork.
competitive_landscape: North Ferry (Greenport ↔ Shelter Island) and South Ferry (North Haven ↔ Shelter Island) are the dominant short-crossing incumbents; Cross Sound Ferry dominates the Orient Point ↔ New London corridor; the Viking Fleet runs the seasonal Montauk ↔ Block Island express. All are diesel, and there is no direct fast passenger link along the South Fork (Sag Harbor ↔ Montauk) today — that, plus the Suffolk County public-ferry study, is the open lane. The competitive alternative for the hero legs is the notoriously congested summer road network, not another boat.

regulatory_note: New York State's clean-transportation and harbor decarbonization push, plus the Suffolk County public-ferry study, create both a regulatory tailwind and a greenfield charging/shore-power window at Sag Harbor's Long Wharf, Greenport's Mitchell Park Marina, and the Shelter Island and Orient terminals.
seasonality: A pronounced summer leisure peak (Memorial Day–Labor Day) driven by the Hamptons second-home and visitor economy, with strong shoulder seasons and a year-round island-resident commuter base on the Shelter Island crossings. Peak-summer road gridlock makes the water alternative most valuable exactly when demand is highest.

navier_fit: High. The East End combines short protected crossings ideal for high-frequency foiling shuttles with mid-range open-water hero legs (Montauk–Block Island, Sag Harbor–Montauk) that sit comfortably inside Pioneer II range and decisively beat summer road congestion. An extreme-wealth leisure market, an active public-ferry study anchored at Sag Harbor, and a greenfield charging window at every terminal align demand, narrative and infrastructure timing.
